did_you_know.text: Did you know? The construction of Solomon’s palace took thirteen years, and when it was completed, it was said that the entire palace had been finished.

Did you know? The House of the Forest of Lebanon was an especially large building: it was one hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, and it rested on four rows of cedar pillars.
Did you know? The House of the Forest of Lebanon had forty-five windows, arranged in three rows—fifteen in each row.
Did you know? The palace buildings were made of costly stones, cut and finished with a saw, both inside and outside.
Did you know? Solomon brought Hiram from Tyre, a man skilled in wisdom, understanding, and the craftsmanship of various works in bronze.
Did you know? Hiram made two large bronze pillars, decorated with capitals, latticework, chains, and pomegranates.
Did you know? The two bronze pillars were set up in the portico of the Temple: Solomon named the right-hand pillar Jachin and the left-hand pillar Boaz.
Did you know? Hiram made the bronze Sea like a round bowl, ten cubits in diameter and five cubits high; it was set on twelve oxen.
Did you know? The Temple had ten stands—bronze structures—each with wheels, decorations, and its own basin.

Did you know? Among the gold furnishings Solomon made were the gold altar, the table for the bread of the Presence, and ten lampstands—five on the right and five on the left before the inner sanctuary.
